report.tagline: A second-hand marketplace from Lithuania where selling is free and buyers pay a small protection fee, now huge in the UK and Europe.
report.simpleSummary: Vinted is an app where you sell clothes, shoes and bits from home that you no longer want. Listing and selling cost the seller nothing. The buyer pays the price plus a small 'buyer protection' fee and postage, and gets a refund if the item never arrives or is not as described. It started in Vilnius in 2008 and is now one of the most downloaded shopping apps in the UK.

overview.whatItDoes: Vinted is a peer-to-peer marketplace: ordinary people sell used items to other people. It started with clothes and now covers shoes, kids' items, books, electronics and home goods. Its big idea is that sellers pay nothing, so people list far more items than on fee-charging sites like eBay or Depop.
howItWorks: A seller takes photos in the app, adds brand, size and condition, picks a price and lists it for free.
Buyers search or browse, 'favourite' items, and can send an offer or bundle several items from one seller.
At checkout the buyer pays the item price, a buyer protection fee of about £0.70 plus 5% of the price in the UK, and postage.
Vinted holds the money until the buyer confirms the item arrived as described, then releases it to the seller's Vinted balance.
The seller ships with a prepaid label or a QR code at a drop-off point, including Vinted's own Vinted Go lockers in some countries.
Sellers can pay to 'Bump' a listing up the feed for a few days, or buy a Wardrobe Spotlight to push their whole shop.
overview.valueProposition: For sellers: turn your wardrobe into cash at no cost. For buyers: branded clothes for a fraction of shop prices, with a refund if something goes wrong.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Sellers list and sell without paying a fee or commission.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Brings in huge supply. More items attract more buyers, which attracts more sellers.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Buyer pays about £0.70 plus 5%; Vinted holds the payment and refunds if there is a problem.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Vinted's main revenue stream and the reason buyers trust strangers.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Prepaid labels, QR drop-off and tracking chosen at checkout.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Removes the hardest part of selling and gives Vinted a margin on postage.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Paid boosts that push a listing or a whole wardrobe higher for a few days.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Second revenue stream that charges keen sellers without taxing casual ones.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Vinted's own lockers and drop-off network in some markets.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Lowers shipping cost per parcel and gives Vinted more control over delivery.

steps.detail: Hears from another parent that selling on Vinted is free.
Photographs a winter coat, picks the brand and size, and lists it at £12.
A buyer offers £10; the parent accepts in chat.
Shows a QR code at a parcel shop; no printer needed.
Buyer marks the item as OK, or two days pass with no complaint.
£10 lands in the Vinted balance and is withdrawn to the bank.
Searches for Levi's 501 jeans in their size.
Checks photos, condition and the seller's reviews.
Adds a second item from the same seller to save on postage.
Pays £18 plus about £1.60 buyer protection and postage.
Item arrives in a few days; buyer confirms it is as described.
Buys a bag of branded items at a car boot sale.
Pays to bump the best ten for more views.
Drops off several parcels each day.
Keeps records because platforms now report sellers above set thresholds to HMRC.

businessModel.summary: Vinted charges buyers, not sellers. Every order carries a buyer protection fee, sellers can pay for boosts, and Vinted earns a margin on shipping. Free selling floods the app with listings, and those listings pull in buyers.

revenueStreams.detail: About £0.70 plus 5% of the item price on every UK order; the largest share of revenue.
Bumps and Wardrobe Spotlight, paid by sellers who want more visibility.
Margin on labels and on Vinted Go lockers.
Ads shown in the app in some markets.

businessModel.pricing: Free to list and sell. UK buyer protection fee about £0.70 plus 5% of the item price. Postage set by the chosen carrier. Bumps from about £1 per item.
costDrivers: TV and online marketing to win buyers in new countries
Trust and safety: fraud checks, dispute handling, fake detection
Building the shipping network, including Vinted Go
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a £20 item in the UK, the buyer pays about £1.70 in buyer protection fee (£0.70 plus 5% of £20). Card payment costs take perhaps £0.30 to £0.40, so Vinted keeps about £1.30 before support and fraud costs. Add a small margin on postage and occasional bumps. Each order earns little, but volume is huge. 2024 revenue of €813 million with about €77 million net profit shows that after marketing and staff, Vinted keeps roughly 9 to 10% of its revenue as profit.

howTheyGetUsers: TV and social ads, especially when entering a new country
Word of mouth: 'I made £200 clearing my wardrobe'
Free selling, which pulls sellers away from eBay and Depop
TikTok and YouTube 'Vinted haul' and reselling videos
whatBringsUsersBack: Thousands of new listings every day in your size and favourite brands
Offers, messages and price-drop alerts on favourited items
Sellers coming back to list the next bag of clothes
Vinted balance money that is easiest to spend on Vinted
growth.moat: Vinted has more second-hand listings than any rival in much of Europe because selling is free. More listings mean buyers find what they want, which brings more sellers. Its own shipping network also lowers costs. A rival would need to match both the free model and the supply at the same time.

northStar.metric: Items sold per month where the buyer confirmed the item as described
northStar.why: Each confirmed sale means a buyer got what they paid for and a seller made money. Counting only confirmed sales filters out disputes and scams, so the metric rises only when the marketplace works for both sides.

improvementIdeas.idea: Show the full price with fee and postage in search results, not only at checkout.
improvementIdeas.problem: Buyers abandon carts when the fee appears at the last step.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer abandoned checkouts and fewer fee complaints.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Checkout drop-off at the fee line

improvementIdeas.idea: Verified seller badge after ID check and 20 clean sales, with faster payouts.
improvementIdeas.problem: Buyers fear scams and fakes from new sellers.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher conversion on badged sellers' listings.

improvementIdeas.idea: Price suggestion based on sold prices of the same brand and size.
improvementIdeas.problem: Sellers guess prices, then wait or get lowballed.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Faster sales and more listings that sell.

improvementIdeas.idea: In-app tax helper that shows sellers their yearly totals against the reporting threshold.
improvementIdeas.problem: Side-hustle sellers are confused by HMRC reporting rules.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer sellers quitting from fear of tax.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Seller return rate after January reporting

pmLessons: Making one side of a marketplace free can grow supply fast. Vinted made selling free and charged buyers instead.
A fee feels fair when it is named as protection. Calling it 'buyer protection' turned a cost into a trust feature.
Owning a slice of logistics, like Vinted Go lockers, can lower cost per order and improve the experience.
A plain, simple product can beat a stylish rival if it is cheaper and easier for the busiest user group.

interviewQuestions.question: Why does Vinted charge buyers and not sellers?
interviewQuestions.hint: Explain supply-side growth and network effects. Compare with eBay and Depop. Note how the 'protection' framing makes buyers accept the fee.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Vinted in the US?
interviewQuestions.hint: List barriers: awareness, shipping costs, competition from Poshmark and Depop. Pick one, propose a feature, and set a metric like new listings per week.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you cut scams on Vinted without slowing honest sales?
interviewQuestions.hint: Name scam types. Ideas: seller verification, payment holds for new accounts, photo checks. Track fraud rate with conversion as a guardrail.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature that helps casual sellers sell faster.
interviewQuestions.hint: Pricing tips from sold data, AI listing from photos, bundle prompts. Measure median days to sale.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Vinted's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Confirmed items sold. Break it into active buyers, live supply, listing conversion and order trust.
